title: TP stability fixes: customer comms + runtime-1.19 release coordination (Dedicated/Enterprise)
creator: Henry Cho
project: Multi-GPU (TP) stability fixes (Serving Runtime Performance: Kernel + Scheduling)
description:
Goal
Coordinate customer-facing comms and release messaging for the TP (tensor parallel) stability work landing in runtime-1.19 (and any patch follow-ups). This ticket is specifically about: (1) what we tell Dedicated + Enterprise customers, (2) setting realistic timeline expectations and rollout shape, and (3) release note wording and Support macros.

Background / why this matters
We have ongoing customer-visible failures under sustained TP load (timeouts / 5xx / hung streams). We are fixing core failure modes (collective async error propagation, cancellation/barrier deadlocks, TP-group watchdog + quarantine, and observability). The technical work is tracked in ENG-2401 umbrella + sub-issues.

This PM workstream needs to be crisp and non-committal on internals (NCCL specifics, kernel details), while being concrete on:
- What symptoms are addressed
- What changes for customers (flags/defaults, tuning guidance, any behavior changes during partial failures)
- Rollout plan (Hosted canary → Dedicated opt-in → default enablement), and how customers can safely participate
- What evidence we will share (metrics improvements, reduced timeouts)

Deliverables
1) Customer email/update template (Dedicated + Enterprise)
- Audience: platform owner / ML eng lead / SRE counterpart
- Tone: direct, operational, action-oriented
- Includes:
  - Summary of fix scope
  - Availability timeline (canary window + opt-in window)
  - What we need from customer to enroll (cluster info, workload patterns, maintenance window, opt-in flag)
  - What success looks like and what we’ll monitor (timeouts/5xx, watchdog/quarantine events, collective latency)
  - Rollback plan / opt-out flag

2) Release notes draft for runtime-1.19 (customer-facing)
- Keep phrasing customer-centric; avoid "we rewrote X".
- Must call out any new config knobs or changed defaults.

3) Support macros + escalation guidance
- Provide:
  - Known-issue synopsis
  - Recommended mitigations pre-fix (traffic shaping, concurrency caps, flag-based mitigations)
  - What logs/metrics to request from customer for triage
  - When to page Runtime vs SRE

4) Dedicated rollout plan summary (customer-facing version)
- Short version to share in a ticket / email:
  - "opt-in first" with guardrails
  - what to watch
  - what qualifies as "resolved" vs "improved"

5) FAQ (internal) for CSM/Sales/Support
- Example questions:
  - "Is this an NCCL issue or Redwood issue?" (answer: we’ve hardened our runtime behavior around collectives and cancellation; no blame)
  - "Will this impact latency/throughput?" (answer: expected neutral; we added lightweight checks + quarantine only on stuck groups)
  - "What happens during quarantine/reset?" (answer: requests may fail fast vs hanging; platform routes away; Dedicated will see transient errors rather than indefinite stalls)
  - "Can we turn it off?" (yes, opt-out flag; guidance)
  - "Do we need a driver update?" (generally no; infra issues are separate, but we’ll validate versions during enrollment)

Proposed customer-facing wording (draft)
Release note bullets (runtime-1.19):
- Improved multi-GPU tensor-parallel stability under sustained load, reducing hangs/timeouts during long-running and streaming generations.
- Added forward-progress watchdogs for tensor-parallel worker groups to detect stalled execution and quarantine unhealthy groups to prevent repeated customer-facing timeouts.
- Improved cancellation handling for streaming disconnects/timeouts to prevent worker-group deadlocks.
- Added additional runtime metrics and structured logs to distinguish communication stalls vs kernel stalls vs scheduler starvation (to speed up RCA and reduce time-to-mitigation).

Important caveats to include (so we don’t surprise customers)
- In some failure scenarios, the system will prefer failing fast over hanging indefinitely (may appear as a short spike in errors while recovery happens).
- Dedicated opt-in recommended first; default enablement will follow after canary confidence.
- We are not changing model outputs; this is runtime stability only.

Timeline (to align with engineering + SRE)
- Hosted:
  - Canary start: once ENG-2406 + ENG-2407 + dashboard alerts (ENG-2408) are in a build that passes perf gates
  - Canary duration: 3–5 days of sustained load coverage (including nightly perf-canary)
- Dedicated:
  - Opt-in: immediately after Hosted canary shows improvement (target 1–2 weeks window)
  - Default-on: gated by PM-513 policy decision + SRE confidence (no date commitments externally; provide range)

Acceptance criteria
- Release notes for runtime-1.19 reviewed by Runtime leads (Sofia/Hiro) + SRE (Sean/Rafael) and approved for publication.
- Support macros posted in Support KB and linked in known-issue page.
- Customer email template finalized and shared with CSM/Support; includes opt-in instructions + rollback/opt-out.
- FAQ posted internally (Sales/CS-friendly) with a single source of truth link.
- Comms explicitly mention which customers are eligible for opt-in and how we will select early adopters (high-TP workloads, recent incidents, willingness to run a maintenance window).

Links
- Umbrella engineering issue: ENG-2401
- Rollout policy decision: PM-513
- Release draft (Confluence): /eng-serving-runtime/release-notes/runtime-1-19-tp-stability-fixes
- Known issue page (Confluence): /eng-serving-runtime/known-issues/tensor-parallel-hang-timeout-known-issue-and-workarounds
- Dashboard spec: /eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/tp-collectives-and-scheduler-health-dashboard

Open questions (need answers before sending to customers)
1) Exact names of new flags + default values by deployment mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private).
2) What’s the customer-visible behavior when quarantine triggers mid-stream? (fail fast vs retry semantics).
3) What are the rollback triggers SRE wants customers to watch for during opt-in?
4) Are we comfortable describing this as "fix" vs "mitigation"? (recommendation: say "improvements" + "reduces" rather than absolute claims).

Owner checklist
- [ ] Collect final flag names/defaults from ENG-2406/2407 owners
- [ ] Confirm canary gates + success metrics with Rafael/Sean
- [ ] Draft customer email + get review from Support (Dev/Owen)
- [ ] Draft FAQ + share with Sales/CS enablement
- [ ] Finalize release notes wording + handoff to Releases (Connor) for publication
